AI response generation, agent decisions, prompt orchestration, model-provider selection, autonomous planning (NXS-P13)
Scheduler (NXS-P15), campaign scheduling / bulk audience selection / mass marketing automation (NXS-P16)

The Customer / Identity / Conversation / participant / timeline model itself — that stays owned by NXS-P06; P09 attaches channel messages to it and never creates a second customer or conversation model
HTTP / OpenAPI / GraphQL execution and the credential vault — those stay owned by the NXS-P07 Integration Hub; P09 reuses the vault seam and never invents a competing secret store
A full media / attachment storage platform — P09 ships only a safe bounded metadata boundary that future storage can extend without coupling
A production external secret vault, real provider accounts / credentials, and production deployment
objective: Implement the permanent Nexus AI enterprise messaging subsystem for WhatsApp (NXS-WA-001), Email (NXS-EMAIL-001) and SMS (NXS-SMS-001), inbound and outbound, on a provider-neutral MessagingProvider abstraction. Inbound pipeline: provider webhook -> channel adapter -> authenticity / signature verification -> tenant + provider-account resolution (fail closed, provider payload never names the trusted organization_id) -> payload-size bound -> provider-payload normalization -> dedupe / replay / idempotency by provider delivery identity -> NXS-P06 customer identity resolution -> NXS-P06 conversation / thread resolution -> normalized message persistence -> P04 transactional outbox event -> provider ACK (a security-invalid webhook is never ACKed as accepted, and no customer / conversation is created before authenticity passes). Outbound pipeline: internal caller -> MessagingService -> organization / channel policy -> conversation + customer validation -> durable outbound idempotency (same org + key + fingerprint replays the prior result; different fingerprint is a deterministic NXS_MSG_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; exactly-once network delivery is NOT claimed; an ambiguous provider timeout is represented honestly and a non-idempotent send is never blindly resent) -> provider adapter -> provider -> normalized provider result -> message state + receipt -> P04 event. Tenant-owned messaging_accounts (channel + provider + external account id + sender identity + credential_ref into the P07 vault seam + status + bounded configuration + webhook metadata) with forced RLS and composite tenant-aware FKs; no cross-Organization phone number / account adoption. Normalized message model (messaging_messages) with organization_id, conversation_id, customer_id, channel, direction, status, provider, provider_account_id, provider_message_id, sender / recipient addresses, content type + safe bounded content, reply_to, correlation_id, idempotency_key, provider + lifecycle timestamps, error_code — no provider secret ever in a message row, an event, or a log. Monotonic delivery state machine (RECEIVED / QUEUED / SENDING / SENT / DELIVERED / READ / FAILED) with per-channel provider-status mapping, impossible-regression rejection and idempotent duplicate-callback handling. Stable NXS_MSG_* RFC 9457 error taxonomy. WhatsApp: provider-neutral boundary with a Meta Cloud API reference adapter, inbound / outbound text, provider message id, address normalization, delivery status, webhook challenge + signature verification, duplicate + replay protection, bounded safe media metadata (provider-supplied MIME / name / type never trusted, no arbitrary provider URL fetch). Email: provider abstraction for inbound / outbound, normalized sender / recipients / cc / bcc / subject / text + bounded HTML (never executed), Message-ID / In-Reply-To / References threading, header-injection + CRLF protection, bounded recipient count, no arbitrary caller headers, inbound webhook authenticity, safe attachment metadata boundary only. SMS: provider-neutral inbound / outbound, normalized E.164 addresses, bounded body, segment metadata where available, tenant-owned sender identity, webhook authenticity, dedupe / replay, outbound idempotency, provider-error normalization, NO OTP semantics. Governed API: POST/GET /api/v1/messaging/messages, messaging account CRUD, and provider-specific inbound webhook routes under /api/v1/webhooks/messaging/{provider} — no raw provider-request / arbitrary-URL / arbitrary-method / arbitrary-header / access-token / raw-SMTP / callback-forwarding surface. New P03 RBAC delta: messaging:read / messaging:send / messaging:manage_accounts (org_member gets read + send only). P04 events messaging.message.received / queued / sent / delivered / read / failed (ID + metadata only, no body where privacy dictates, no secrets). Proven by unit, integration, per-channel (WhatsApp / Email / SMS), security, concurrency and resilience test matrices, reversible migration with forced RLS + tenant-aware FKs, tenant schema guard, multi-architecture build and clean-room on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. Explicit lifecycle / contract guards keep NXS-P10 / P13 / P14 / P16 PLANNED and untouched.
